title: Connections: Ecosystem
desc: Find the natural thread linking each set of clues

questions.q: What connects: the dodo, the thylacine, and the passenger pigeon?
questions.a: All went extinct due to human activity — the dodo (hunting, 1681), thylacine/Tasmanian tiger (hunting, 1936), passenger pigeon (hunting and habitat loss, 1914). All three have active de-extinction research

questions.q: Odd one out: dolphin, whale, seal, shark. Which and why?
questions.a: Shark — it's the only fish. Dolphins, whales, and seals are all mammals that breathe air, give live birth, and nurse their young

questions.q: What connects: coral, mushrooms, and lichen?
questions.a: None of them are what most people think — coral is an animal (not a plant), mushrooms are fungi (not plants), and lichen is a symbiosis of fungus + alga (not a single organism)

questions.q: Put these in order of lifespan, shortest to longest: mayfly, tortoise, human, bowhead whale
questions.a: Mayfly (24 hours as adults) → human (~80 years) → tortoise (~150-200 years) → bowhead whale (over 200 years, possibly the longest-lived mammal)

questions.q: What connects: a Venus flytrap, a sundew, and a pitcher plant?
questions.a: They're all carnivorous plants — they trap and digest insects to supplement nutrients in poor soil

questions.q: What connects: the Amazon, the Congo, and the Daintree?
questions.a: Three of the world's most significant rainforests — South America, Central Africa, and Australia respectively

questions.q: True, false, or it depends: 'Daddy longlegs are the most venomous spiders but their fangs are too small to bite humans'
questions.a: False on every level — the common 'daddy longlegs' (harvestmen) aren't even spiders, and cellar spiders (also called daddy longlegs) have weak venom that's harmless to humans. The whole thing is a myth

questions.q: What connects: a caterpillar inside a chrysalis literally dissolves into soup before becoming a butterfly. What's the scientific term?
questions.a: Metamorphosis — specifically holometabolism. The caterpillar's body breaks down almost entirely into a cellular soup, then reorganises using 'imaginal discs' as blueprints

questions.q: Odd one out: eagle, penguin, ostrich, kiwi. Which and why?
questions.a: Eagle — it's the only one that can fly. Penguins, ostriches, and kiwis are all flightless birds

questions.q: What connects: wolves in Yellowstone, beavers in the UK, and lynx in Spain?
questions.a: All are rewilding success stories — wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone (1995), beavers to the UK (2009 onwards), and the Iberian lynx was brought back from the brink of extinction through breeding programmes
